title: Positioning mode: niche differentiation or category-buyer distinctiveness
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Whether to position for a niche segment (Dunford) or for all category buyers with distinctive assets and buying-situation links (Sharp, Romaniuk).
applies_when: Choosing who to target and how to describe the business
exclusions: Owner has already chosen a target segment for a stated reason (record it; mode is advisory)
required_inputs: How buyers choose (memory in the moment vs comparison)
evidence_requirements: number of viable substitutes buyers see as interchangeable
existing brand cues the business already uses consistently
Candidate CEPs from VoC snippets, reviews and sales notes that mention the moment of need
Search queries that express situations (Search Console, Google Business Profile queries, keyword research)
Optional: pick-any survey of category buyers in the service area (customers and non-customers) with CEPs as rows and brands as columns, plus 'none'
Source-of-business at intake ('what did you use or buy before', 'who else did you call')
Rough size proxies for competitors (locations, review counts; low confidence)
Customer profile (area, age band or firm size) versus the category's
missing_data_behavior: Unknown buying mode: default by business type and label it.

decision_branches.if: Consumer repeat-purchase or everyday local service
decision_branches.then: Category-buyer mode by default: reach all buyers, link to many buying situations, swap test advisory.

decision_branches.if: Niche B2B, capacity-limited service or early-stage product
decision_branches.then: Niche mode by default; Sharp's laws are contextual heuristics.

decision_branches.if: New customers come mostly from the biggest rivals
decision_branches.then: Normal (duplication of purchase); don't over-target one rival.

implementation_steps: Classify the category on the conditions above
Pick a mode and say why
In both modes run a brand-cue audit: which cues (name, colour, logo, character, tagline, style) the business uses and whether they are consistent across site, pack, posts and ads
If budget allows, test fame and uniqueness of 1-2 assets with category buyers
In category-buyer mode, the swap test is advisory, not a gate
Assign each BK10 framework a status: default / heuristic / set aside
Pass statuses into the plan brief so agents cite them with the right strength
Generate CEPs with why, when, where, with whom and with what, in buyer words and before any brand
Rank by commonness (how often linked to any brand, VoC counts, search volume)
Map existing posts, pages and ads to CEPs; find neglected common CEPs
Add a source-of-business field at intake
Tally sources against rough competitor size
dependencies: A defined category and the brands buyers would actually know, including the biggest
For measurement: a sample of category buyers, not only customers
Enough intake answers to read a pattern (the book gives no threshold; label small n)

cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: fame = share linking asset to brand; uniqueness = share of those linking it only to this brand

metrics: share of plans where status was set
Mental market share = brand's CEP links / all brands' CEP links
Mental penetration = category buyers linking the brand to at least one CEP / all category buyers surveyed
Network size = brand's CEP links / buyers linking the brand to at least one CEP
Share of content by CEP over the last 4-8 weeks (ClimbOS proxy)
Share of new customers by previous provider
Share of lost deals by destination
guardrails: Neither author's preference is a hard restriction.
Brand-science benchmarks are dated consumer-panel data.
Never fabricate competitor gaps to create differentiation (existing BK03 rule)
Don't recommend a rebrand or new visual identity without evidence the current assets lack fame
Never cite a BK10 law as certain for niche B2B, capacity-limited or pre-launch businesses (owner decision 2026-10-20)
Never survey only customers and call it market mental availability
No invented CEP statistics; label n
Don't drop a CEP just because it is 'parity' in consumer repeat categories
Don't build strategy around one competitor from a handful of anecdotes
Don't claim competitor shares without a source
alternatives_when_constrained: No survey budget: audit consistency only and ask 5-10 customers what they recall
No brand cues yet: pick simple ones and keep them (social-visual-briefs provisional kit)
Unknown dimensions: ask the 1-3 dimension questions (scoring.ts dimensionsToConfirm) before applying any default
No survey: use the share of situation queries where the business appears (Search Console impressions) as a low-confidence proxy
No VoC: start from search queries and reviews of category leaders
No intake data: use reviews and sales notes mentioning previous providers, labelled anecdotal
stop_conditions: Revisit mode when evidence of a best-fit pattern appears, or when the business moves from niche to mass category
If network size doesn't rise after two campaign waves on a new CEP, check branding (could viewers tell whose ad it was?) and reach before changing the message
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Using 'everyone' as an excuse to skip customer research
Sharp's evidence on low perceived differentiation is from mature consumer categories and retail banks; may not hold for new B2B tools
Hybrid businesses (B2B2C, marketplaces) need per-side treatment
Single-occasion categories (emergency locksmith) where breadth matters little
Tiny service areas where survey samples are too small
Size proxies like review counts are weak

contextual_heuristic.rule: proposed rule: positioning skill selects a mode (niche-differentiation or category-buyer) from category conditions and records why
proposed rule: in category-buyer mode, 'all category buyers in the service area' is an acceptable segment and the swap test is advisory
proposed: A mental availability reading from customers only is labelled biased and not reported as market mental availability.
proposed: For a new brand, a rare or unique CEP is not the main launch message unless the business is deliberately niche or capacity-limited.
proposed: Competitor teardowns rank competitors by size or penetration proxies as the default main source of customers, and flag a 'closest rival' only with switching evidence.
proposed: A skewed customer profile is first checked for distribution, price or variant restrictions before being explained as positioning.

strategic_preference.rule: proposed rule: every positioning output includes a brand-cue consistency check across site, posts and ads
proposed rule: compute a BK10 applicability status per plan from customerType, frequency, salesMotion, capacity and customer count; agents must phrase BK10 claims at that strength
proposed: Content, ad and page plans tag each piece with one buying situation (CEP), and a 4-8 week calendar covers several common CEPs rather than one claim repeated.

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed rule: asset fame/uniqueness claims require survey data; otherwise label as unmeasured
proposed: Mental market share, mental penetration and network size are computed in code from a pick-any grid with n shown; the model never estimates them.
proposed: Source-of-business (previous provider) is captured at intake as a standard field.

unknown_to_investigate.rule: proposed rule: which mode wins for early-stage local consumer brands is unknown; track outcomes by mode in bench
proposed rule: whether double jeopardy holds for small SaaS categories is unknown; collect owner data in bench before using it as a default

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed rule: when capacity utilisation >= 0.8 (diagnosis.ts), penetration-growth advice is suppressed

external_requirement.rule: proposed rule: in sales-led niche B2B, translate 'reach all buyers' into list coverage of the reachable account universe using only owner-sourced or public data (no assumed prospect database)
